newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African strike seen limited in Cape Town.
newsitem.headline: South African strike seen limited in Cape Town.

text.p: Support for the 24-hour general strike called by the Congress of South African Trade Unions appeared limited in Cape Town early on Monday but more workers were expected to down tools for a rally on the Grand Parade at midday.
The Port of Cape Town reported that shipping had not been affected although some workers had stayed away.
"In the break-bulk division only 16 out of 66 people booked turned up but everything seems okay in the port cartage division," a spokesman told Reuters.
"The container division is also all okay but they did have some delays earlier this morning because stevedores were not available and they had to arrange casual labour."
All appeared normal at the Caltex refinery in Milnerton as well but all employers said that they would not have a clear indication of the extent of the stay-away until the rally was held.
"Some staff might leave later in the morning to go to the Grand Parade," one employer said.
At the Sapref refinery in Durban, only about 10 of the 850 workforce stayed away on Monday and operations were not affected.
